---
title: "Methods"
---

These notes explain implementation choices that are hard to read from the code. The
Methods section of the manuscript is the authoritative description.

## Model

Each site has one XGBoost regressor per cross-validation fold, with target `NEP_ZSCORE` and predictors `TA_ZSCORE`,
`SWIN_ZSCORE`, `VPD_ZSCORE` and `SWC_ZSCORE`. The settings are in `src/models.py`:

```python
n_estimators=3000
max_depth=6
learning_rate=0.05
tree_method='hist'
subsample=0.8
colsample_bytree=0.8
reg_lambda=1.0
reg_alpha=0.1
gamma=0.2
min_child_weight=5
early_stopping_rounds=100
random_state=42
```

Within each fold, 15 percent of the training records serve as the early-stopping set. The published run uses these settings (`TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS = False` in script 31). With
`True`, script 31 runs a randomized search instead of the SHAP calculation. The search tests 25 of the 125 combinations of `n_estimators` 2000 to
4000, `max_depth` 4 to 8 and `learning_rate` 0.01 to 0.1 per site (`TUNE_N_ITER`).

## Flux targets

| Target | Source variable | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| `NEP_ZSCORE` | `NEE_VUT_50`, sign flipped | Measured, quality flag 0 only |
| `GPP_ZSCORE` | `GPP_NT_VUT_50` | Partitioning product |
| `RECO_ZSCORE` | `RECO_NT_VUT_50` | Partitioning product |
| `ET_ZSCORE` | derived from `LE_F_MDS` | Includes gap-filled values |

Where the first-choice variable is missing, script 13 takes the next available one:
`NEE_CUT_50` at 14 sites, `GPP_NT_CUT_50` and `RECO_NT_CUT_50` at 16 sites, and the daytime
partitioning (`*_DT_VUT_50`, `*_DT_CUT_50`) at 17 sites (`NEE_VAR`, `GPP_VAR` and `RECO_VAR`
in the site table).

Median out-of-sample R^2^ across the 208 sites: NEP 0.64, GPP 0.67, RECO 0.58, ET 0.67.
With nighttime partitioning (191 sites), RECO comes from a temperature response fitted to nighttime NEE and extrapolated into the
day, and GPP is RECO minus NEE. Part of any temperature signal in their attribution
therefore belongs to the partitioning. The LE quality filter is disabled in
`src/files.py`, because the FLUXNET flag marks every LE record as gap-filled.

## Cross-validation

`CV_STRATEGY` in script 31 selects the split. `random`, used for the published results, is a shuffled 5-fold split. `blocked` holds
out one calendar year at a time and skips sites with a single year. With `blocked`, over
206 sites, the median out-of-sample R^2^ falls from 0.64 to 0.54. The Stage 8 VPD
contribution is unchanged (-0.429 in both), and the soil water contribution weakens from
-0.085 to -0.064.

## Predictor sets

`FEATURE_SET` in script 31 selects `full`, `no_vpd` or `no_ta`. Removing either variable
lowers the score at 205 of 208 sites (median R^2^ 0.64 for `full`, 0.60 for `no_vpd`, 0.61
for `no_ta`). When one variable
is removed, the other takes over part of its role. The attributions in the full model therefore
are conditional on both being present. The `no_ta` run goes through the full aggregation
and is one row of Table 1. With models that never saw temperature, the threshold is
1.28 kPa [1.19, 1.37], against 1.26 kPa [1.16, 1.36] for the full model. A model with TA
and relative humidity was not fitted. VPD follows from TA and relative humidity, and such a
model holds the same information as one with TA and VPD and cannot separate heat from
dryness any better.

## SHAP

SHAP values come from `TreeExplainer` with `feature_perturbation="tree_path_dependent"`,
which retains the observed joint distribution of TA and VPD. The result is a conditional
attribution of the fitted prediction among correlated predictors, not a separation of
physiological causes. The values are out-of-sample: each fold explains only the
20 percent of records its model never trained on.

## ALE

ALE curves come from `PyALE.ale` with `grid_size=100` per predictor (100 quantile intervals, up to 101 points per curve). Each site has one
model fitted on 85 percent of the records, separate from the cross-validated models
behind the SHAP values. ALE and SHAP interrogate models of the same form on the same
data. Their agreement therefore tests the interpretation method, not the physiology.

## Soil water layer {#soil-water-layer}

The published analysis uses `SWC_F_MDS_1`, the shallowest layer, at 207 sites. CA-Obs has no layer 1 and uses `SWC_F_MDS_2` in all runs. With
`SWC_LAYER = "deepest"`, script 21 takes at each site the deepest layer that holds at
least 90 percent of the records of layer 1 within the peak months
(`src/common.py::deepest_swc_per_site`). With this coverage floor, 106 of the 128 sites have the same number of records in
both runs, and no site has fewer than 90 percent of its shallow-run records. Without it, a deeper but gappier layer would have shrunk the sample at some
sites.

Under this rule, 127 of 208 sites move to a deeper layer (layers 2 to 9), CA-Obs remains on
layer 2 and 80 sites remain on layer 1. A `deep-sm` run therefore includes all 208 sites,
and 81 of them are bit-identical to the shallow run. `SITE_SUBSET = "deeper-only"` restricts
both runs to the 128 sites below layer 1, which gives the matched pair (CA-Obs is the same in
both). Depths in centimeters cannot be recovered from
the data products.

At Stage 8, the ratio of the VPD to the soil water attribution is 5.03 (shallow) and 4.86
(deep) over all 208 sites, and 4.22 and 4.00 on the matched 128. Only 10 of 30 evergreen
broadleaf sites have a usable deeper layer.

## Stress stages

`src/stages.py` defines nine record subsets on z-scores. The cut-offs are 0.319 (middle
25 percent), 0.714 (middle 52.5 percent) and 1.282 (outer 10 percent) of a standard normal.

| Stage | Condition |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | all records |
| 1 | TA, VPD and SWC within the middle 25 percent |
| 2 | warm, soil moisture normal, VPD not extreme |
| 3 | warm, dry soil, VPD not extreme |
| 4 | hot, dry soil, VPD not extreme |
| 5 | hot, very dry soil, VPD not extreme |
| 6 | extremely hot, very dry soil, VPD not extreme |
| 7 | extremely hot, extremely dry soil, VPD not extreme |
| 8 | extremely hot, extremely dry soil, extremely dry air |

Standardization does not make the drivers Gaussian. Script 87 measures the empirical
share of records below each cut-off. At the median site, this share is within six
percentage points of the Gaussian share, and within 2.2 at the Stage 8 cut-offs. The
stages do not constrain shortwave radiation, which rises from 0.34σ at Stage 1 to 0.65σ
at Stage 8 (script 45). The sequence is not a factorial design. Three tests address
this: the mirrored stage order, the matched records and the factorial cells.

### Stage order

`mirror_1` to `mirror_8` in `src/stages.py` swap the roles of VPD and soil water. VPD
escalates through the stages, and extreme soil dryness comes last. Stage 8 holds the same
records in both orders. Script 88 compares the two orders:

| Order | Second to last stage | Final stage | Cost of the last step |
|---|---|---|---|
| published, extreme VPD last | -0.07 | -0.36 | -0.29 |
| mirrored, extreme soil dryness last | -0.24 | -0.36 | -0.12 |

The mirrored Stage 7 holds about twenty times more records than the published one,
because extreme heat comes with extreme VPD far more often than with extreme soil dryness.

### Record matching

Within the cut-offs, Stage 8 records are hotter, drier and brighter than Stage 7
records. Script 89 pairs every Stage 8 record of a site with the closest Stage 7 record
of the same site, with replacement, within 0.5σ in TA, SWC and SWIN. The strict variant
also requires the same calendar month and an hour of day within one hour. Script 59
writes the summary as part b of Supplementary Table 5.

| | Strict | Covariates only | Unmatched, same sites |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sites with pairs, of 145 with both stages | 140 | 144 | 145 |
| Stage 8 records matched | 60 % | 81 % | |
| Difference after matching, TA, SWC, SWIN, VPD (σ) | +0.15, -0.02, +0.04, +0.98 | +0.14, -0.01, +0.01, +1.09 | |
| Net effect difference, median site (σ) | -0.26 | -0.31 | -0.27 (mean) |
| Sites with a negative net difference | 91 % | 94 % | 83 % |
| VPD contribution difference, median site (σ) | -0.21 | -0.23 | |
| TA, SWC, SWIN contribution differences (σ) | -0.03, 0.00, -0.02 | -0.02, 0.00, -0.02 | |

Shortwave radiation is balanced after matching. The residual TA imbalance of 0.15σ
contributes 0.03σ through the TA attribution.

### Factorial cells

`FACTORIAL_CELLS` in `src/stages.py` crosses four soil water classes with four VPD
classes, at the same cut-offs as the stages. TA is unconstrained. Class 0 is the middle
25 percent. Classes 1 to 3 step toward stress at 0.714 and 1.282, downward for soil water
and upward for VPD. Records with wet soil or low VPD fall in no cell. Script 44 with
`STAGE_SEQUENCE = "factorial"` aggregates the sixteen cells into its own
`factorial-cells/` folder. Script 69 writes Supplementary Table 10. For each cell, it
gives the sites, the records, and the SM, VPD and net effects as the mean of the site
means, with the interquartile range across sites.

With the other driver in its central range, the VPD effect at extreme VPD (-0.40σ) is
about five times the SM effect at extreme SM (-0.08σ). Each effect is nearly the same in
every class of the other driver: -0.40σ at extreme VPD in all four soil water classes,
and -0.08σ at extreme soil water in all four VPD classes.

### Stage 8 by site

Part a of Supplementary Table 5 (script 59) raises the minimum number of Stage 8 records
per site from 1 to 100. For each minimum, it reports the remaining sites, their mean VPD
and SM effects, and the ratio of the two with a bootstrap interval over sites. Two rows
compare the effects within each site, each effect being the mean over the Stage 8
records at that site: the share of sites at which the VPD effect is more negative than the SM effect,
and the median across sites of the VPD minus SM effect. Without a minimum, the VPD
effect is more negative at 146 of 160 sites (91 percent), and the median difference is
-0.37σ.

## Aggregation across sites

Each site contributes one curve or one binned grid, with equal weight. An aggregated bin
is kept where at least half the sites have data. The total standard deviation combines the within-site and between-site variance (law of
total variance, `src/stages.py`). Bars in the stage figures show the standard error of
the site means.

## Threshold definition

The threshold is the highest VPD at which the fitted VPD contribution crosses from
positive to negative. For SHAP (script 54), a fourth-order polynomial is fitted to the
cross-site median per cell of the TA by VPD grid, one point per cell. For ALE (script 46),
a fourth-order polynomial is fitted to each site curve. Its highest crossing from positive
to negative, found as for SHAP, is the site threshold. The ALE threshold is the mean of these
per-site crossings with a t-based 95 percent interval. The mean covers 207 sites, since
US-Cwt has no such crossing. Script 46 also writes the crossing of the pooled mean curve (0.107σ, against 0.192σ for the
mean of the site crossings).

Only crossings from positive to negative count (`src/fit.py`). Over the modeled records of
a site, the VPD attributions average close to zero (median across sites 0.01σ), which
makes a sign change likely at every site but does not set its direction. Script 82
averages each driver's
attribution per 0.1σ bin of that driver and writes, per site and driver, the sign of the
correlation between bin and mean attribution (`82_INFO_DriverEffectDirection.csv`). The
VPD effect decreases at 202 of the 208 sites, while the SW effect increases at all 208.
The TA and SM effects decrease at about half of the sites and increase at the rest.

Script 81 separates four points of the VPD contribution: its peak (0.47 kPa), its zero
crossing (1.26 kPa), its steepest decline (1.50 kPa) and its minimum. It flags points within 2 percent
of the range edge. The minimum is flagged in every group, because the curve is still
falling where the data end. Script 81 reads all points from a 2000-point grid of the fit.
Script 54 places the peak marker of Fig. 4 with `src/fit.py::peak_of_polynomial`, which
takes the maximum from the roots of the derivative and therefore does not depend on the
grid spacing. Both agree at two decimals.

### Conversion to kPa

Per site, `VPD_kPa = (site mean VPD + z * site SD) / 10`, with mean and SD over the
records the models saw. The site values are then averaged with equal weight. A forest
type value is the mean over its sites. Interval bounds go through the same conversion.
CD-Ygb stores VPD in Pa and is divided by 100 first. Without this step, the all-sites
threshold moves from 1.26 to 2.19 kPa.

### Estimator sensitivity

Script 47 re-estimates the threshold under 23 settings: polynomial degrees 2 to 6,
LOWESS at five bandwidths, smoothing splines over two orders of magnitude, four bin widths
and five fitting ranges. All estimates fall between 1.23 and 1.30 kPa. The published fit
is near the median. LOWESS and the second-order polynomial give the lowest values,
0.155 to 0.174σ.

The GAM row of Table 1 fits a cubic B-spline basis with 12 degrees of freedom.
Generalized cross-validation picks the penalty. The intercept enters unpenalized, because
the basis omits its first column and would otherwise pin the fit to zero at the lowest
bin.

### Leave-one-site-out

Script 47 removes each site in turn and refits. The threshold ranges from 1.253 to
1.268 kPa (median 1.264 kPa), and the largest shift is 0.010 kPa (US-CMW). Table 1
reports the range, because each of the 208 values uses 207 of the same 208 sites and the values are
therefore not independent.

### Site VPD range

A site with a narrow VPD range reaches +3σ at a modest absolute VPD. No site has a maximum VPD below
1.25 kPa (lowest site maximum 1.69 kPa). Script 82 therefore splits the sites into
quartiles of their maximum VPD:

| Quartile | n | Median max VPD (kPa) | Threshold (σ) | Threshold (kPa) | Sites with a crossing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lowest | 52 | 2.90 | 0.25 | 1.00 | 52 |
| Q2 | 52 | 3.60 | 0.29 | 1.15 | 52 |
| Q3 | 52 | 4.37 | 0.17 | 1.34 | 51 |
| highest | 52 | 5.69 | 0.04 | 1.41 | 52 |

US-Cwt (Q3) has no crossing from positive to negative. It remains in its quartile and is
left out of the medians.

From the lowest to the highest quartile, the median site maximum VPD grows by 96 percent
and the threshold by 41 percent. The threshold is therefore neither fixed nor
proportional to the site maximum.

### Forest type comparison

The threshold intervals in Figure 4 come from the prediction band of the aggregated curve. Script 49 fits
one threshold per site and compares the distributions over the 207 sites with a crossing
from positive to negative (Kruskal-Wallis H = 11.43, p = 0.010). After Holm correction,
only ENF against DBF differs (p = 0.035). The
forest type medians span 0.19σ, and the widest within-type interquartile range is 0.52σ.

### Regional subsets and record length

Scripts 83 and 84 recompute the threshold as the median of the per-site thresholds, with
Europe, North America or both removed (script 83), and with minimum record lengths of
1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 years (script 84). Table 1 and Supplementary Fig. 4 (script 47) have the same tests on the
aggregated curve, which is the estimator the manuscript reports.

## ERA5 climate normals {#era5-climate-normals}

Script 17 gives each site a 1991 to 2020 mean annual temperature (MAT) and precipitation
(MAP). The values describe the sites in Fig. 1b and Supplementary Table 1 and enter no
analysis.

The first source is the ERA5 file of the flux product (TA_ERA, P_ERA), which ONEFlux
scales to the site measurements. ERA5-Land at the site coordinates (Copernicus CDS,
script 16d) replaces it in these cases:

| Case | MAT | MAP | Sites |
|---|---|---|---|
| No ERA5 file in the flux product (FLUXNET2015 downloads) | yes | yes | 18 |
| No site precipitation, and P_ERA is therefore not scaled (`ERA_SLOPE` of P is -9999 in the BIF or AUXMETEO file) | | yes | 18 |
| P_ERA more than 25% off the MAP reported for the site, ERA5-Land closer | | yes | 29 |
| Set by hand in `config/site_climate_source_override.csv` (ERA5-Land closer to the reported MAT) | yes | | 7 |

The site-reported values come from `config/site_climate_reported_manual.csv` (network pages
and site papers, with sources), the `CLIM_AVG` rows of the site BIF, and the AmeriFlux site
table in `config/`. They serve only for these checks. Four coastal sites (JP-Ynf, US-HB2,
US-HB3, VU-Coc) fall on an ERA5-Land sea cell and use the nearest land cell
(`ERA5_LAND_POINT_OVERRIDE` in script 16d). The output table lists the source of each
value and, for ERA5-Land, the reason (`ERA5_MAT_SOURCE`, `ERA5_MAT_REASON`,
`ERA5_MAP_SOURCE`, `ERA5_MAP_REASON`). Script 51 retains these columns in the Fig. 1 data
file. Script 91 copies that file to the Source Data as `SupplementaryTable1_climate.csv`
and the full table of script 17 as `SupplementaryTable1_climate_full.csv`.
